paraphrase: Great Vajradhara, Tilo, Nāro, Marpa, Mila, and lord of Dharma Gampopa; Karmapa, knower of the three times, and the holders of the four great and eight lesser lineages … to you we pray: hold us with your blessing, we who keep your practice lineage.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Content high; verse divisions as usually printed.

paraphrase: Revulsion is said to be the feet of meditation: to this meditator without attachment to food and wealth, who has cut the ties to this life, grant your blessing that attachment to honour and gain may cease.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: Devotion is said to be the head of meditation: to this meditator who prays constantly to the guru who opens the treasury of oral instructions, grant your blessing that uncontrived devotion may arise.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: Non-distraction is said to be the main body of meditation: to this meditator who rests, without contrivance, in the fresh essence of whatever thought arises, grant your blessing that meditation may be free of mental fabrication.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: The essence of thought is said to be dharmakāya — nothing whatever, yet arising as anything: to this meditator for whom it arises unceasingly, grant your blessing that the inseparability of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa may be realized.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.
